title: The Thief and His Mother
text:
A schoolboy stole a writing tablet from a classmate and carried it home to his mother. She did not punish him or send him back with it. Instead she praised him for his cleverness.

Encouraged, he next brought home a cloak he had taken, and again she approved. As he grew into a young man his thefts grew with him, from small things to things of real value, until at last he was caught in the act. His hands were bound behind his back and he was led away to be executed.

His mother followed in the crowd, weeping and beating her breast. The young man asked the guards to let him say something to her in private. When she leaned close, he seized her ear in his teeth and bit it hard.

She cried out that he was a monster of a son. He answered that if she had punished him the first time he brought home that stolen tablet, he would never have ended where he was now, being led to a shameful death.
lesson: Small wrongs that a child gets away with become habits. Correcting them early, even when it is unpleasant, is a kindness to the adult they will become.
